summary:
Ghosts of Space is an educational storytelling website built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 titled "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars." 
Ghosts of Space looks at five pieces of space hardware: Sojourner, Spirit, Ingenuity, the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle and NEAR Shoemaker. This project does not just list these objects; it walks visitors through short chapter‑style tales that explain why each one was built what it did how it helped science and what it has left behind.
 Ghosts of Space is meant for kids in school and, for anyone who loves space. This website offers an archive of artifacts, a timeline of missions and a text‑to‑speech voice so the stories can be heard as well as read. The project was made with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Its goal is to make the past of old space hardware easy to explore and to understand.
details:
Ghosts of Space is an interactive educational storytelling web experience that chronicles the "retired" NASA hardware resting on the Moon, Mars, and asteroids long after their active missions have concluded.

How It Works

  • Explore the Archive: Visitors start on a sleek landing page featuring an archive of five iconic artifacts: Sojourner, Spirit, Ingenuity, the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, and NEAR Shoemaker.
  • Chapter-Based Storytelling: Selecting an artifact launches a curated, multi-chapter narrative detailing its journey, discoveries, and final resting place.
  • Interactive Navigation & Audio: Users can seamlessly navigate across chapters, browse an interactive mission timeline, and click a built-in audio button to listen to the story via browser-based text-to-speech.

Intended Impact

Designed primarily for students and casual space enthusiasts, the project transforms space exploration history from static dates into an accessible, human-centered narrative. It emphasizes a core truth of spaceflight: even when hardware goes silent, its scientific discoveries and engineering legacy endure.

Technology Stack

Built entirely with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, the prototype is lightweight, responsive, and runs natively in the browser without requiring a backend database or external APIs for its core features.

Future Roadmap

  • Expanded Archive: Adding more verified hardware stories (e.g., Cassini, Opportunity, or Voyager).
  • Richer Media & Citations: Integrating high-resolution NASA archival imagery alongside direct primary-source references for each mission.
  • Enhanced Accessibility: Expanding keyboard navigation, screen-reader optimizations, and customizable text/audio controls.
